units.text: INT. GHOSTS - CONTINUOUS
Well, what do you say of that man now, Mrs. Alving? That was a very different account of matters, was it not?
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Yes, it certainly was.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: It only shows how excessively careful one ought to be in judging one's fellow creatures. But what a heartfelt joy it is to ascertain that one has been mistaken! Don't you think so?
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: I think you are, and will always be, a great baby, Manders.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: I?
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Laying her two hands upon his shoulders.
And I say that I have half a mind to put my arms round your neck, and kiss you.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Stepping hastily back.
No, no! God bless me! What an idea!
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: With a smile.
Oh, you needn't be afraid of me.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: By the table.
You have sometimes such an exaggerated way of expressing yourself. Now, let me just collect all the documents, and put them in my bag.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: He does so.
There, that's all right. And now, good-bye for the present. Keep your eyes open when Oswald comes back. I shall look in again later.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: He takes his hat and goes out through the hall door.
Sighs, looks for a moment out of the window, sets the room in order a little, and is about to go into the dining-room, but stops at the door with a half-suppressed cry.
Oswald, are you still at table?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: In the dining room.
I'm only finishing my cigar.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: I thought you had gone for a little walk.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: In such weather as this?
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: A glass clinks.
MRS. ALVING leaves the door open, and sits down with her knitting on the sofa by the window.
Wasn't that Pastor Manders that went out just now?
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Yes; he went down to the Orphanage.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: H'm.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: The glass and decanter clink again.
With a troubled glance.
Dear Oswald, you should take care of that liqueur. It is strong.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: It keeps out the damp.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Wouldn't you rather come in here, to me?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: I mayn't smoke in there.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: You know quite well you may smoke cigars.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Oh, all right then; I'll come in. Just a tiny drop more first. There!
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: He comes into the room with his cigar, and shuts the door after him.
A short silence.
Where has the pastor gone to?
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: I have just told you; he went down to the Orphanage.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Oh, yes; so you did.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: You shouldn't sit so long at table, Oswald.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Holding his cigar behind him.
But I find it so pleasant, mother.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Strokes and caresses her.
Just think what it is for me to come home and sit at mother's own table, in mother's room, and eat mother's delicious dishes.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: My dear, dear boy!
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Somewhat impatiently, walks about and smokes.
